# Collection, auction and public-catalogue expansion — 27 October 2026

## Result

The atlas now contains **636 source-linked research records**, **529 earliest-title display records**, and **400 editable interpretive SVGs**. The previous published pass had 259 records/158 SVGs: this pass adds **377 net records** and **242 net SVGs** after reconciliation. **236 explicit SVG slots remain empty**. The records include **127 painting candidates** and **116 unresolved creation dates**; these known unknowns are deliberately visible. There are **189 blue-tagged records**, including **144 with SVGs**, across all versions. Title-derived tags and unreviewed colors remain disclosed.

These counts include painted reliefs, panel installations, explicitly marked painting groups, and candidates. They are not a certified count of unique finished paintings. Default earliest-title selection retains Roman numerals and hides later versions only from that display; the linked gallery shows all versions.

## Three checks

1. **Source census:** every imported source row survives exactly once in the assembled ledger. Numbered publication sections and accessible artist inventories are reconciled to their stated counts; exclusions remain reviewable.
2. **Independent identity/metadata review:** separate researchers check dates, media, dimensions, canonical IDs, collection claims and cross-source matches. Corrections include signature years mistakenly resembling EK numbers, contradictory inch/cm conversions, floor thickness versus plan size, historical title aliases, and same physical work with conflicting date reports. Historical lenders never replace stronger current museum records. Ambiguous identities stay separate.
3. **Vector and browser review:** **37 automated checks pass /0 fail**. SVGs are rendered and visually checked against inspected references. They contain editable vector shapes with color tags, accessible titles and provenance, with no raster/script. White painted support is retained; surrounding wall, frame and cast shadows are omitted. Gallery tests cover loading, color filtering, comparable size, shared physical scale, detail/source histories and recoloring.

Curves and vivid screen colors are approximate, not calibrated facsimiles. Unknown physical size, framed/per-panel dimensions and schematic projections do not silently enter true-scale comparison. Normalized-only studies remain available at comparable size.

## Honest stopping conditions

The identified public leads have been followed to documented outcomes, including failures. This does **not** establish that all collections or all auction history are exhausted. Sotheby's loading boundary leaves 80 contemporary cards unreadable; Christie's 334 print-category objects were not individually inspected. Some museum search systems, images and publication downloads return 403/429/504 or migrated 404 pages. A negative indexed query does not prove absent holdings.

The authoritative Bois volumes cover 1940–1953 and 1954–1958. Their complete inventories remain unaccessed through authenticated/library access; public descriptions and sample spreads cannot substitute for them. The complete 135-page 1973 MoMA book's 49 captioned painting plates are represented; a separate full 1973 checklist was not acquired. The 1992 Years in France and full 1979 historical checklist also remain reconciliation boundaries where a complete readable source was not obtained. SFPL/LINK+ ISBN/title checks did not establish a Bois holding or digital entitlement; interlibrary loan is a librarian-assisted possibility, not confirmed access. See the local Bois-access audit.

Unknown inventory totals and missing counts remain null. Missing EK integers are not invented paintings. Metadata, source links, conflicts, historical credits, exclusions and the SVG studies are preserved for the next authoritative reconciliation.
